note: Float @mod with operands of opposite sign where the LLVM lowering frem(frem(a, b) + b, b) and the self-hosted backend round differently (e.g. @mod(-2^-24 as f16, 1.0) is 0 under LLVM and the model, 1.0 under stage2_x86_64). The model follows the LLVM lowering, so this is a backend divergence on a legal input, in every optimize mode.

f80 @min(-0.0, +0.0) and @max(-0.0, +0.0): the model and LLVM order the signed zeros, stage2_x86_64 returns the other zero. The language leaves the order of signed zeros unspecified, so this may be a model over-specification rather than a backend defect.
An i4 read from a packed union and returned is not sign-extended by stage2_x86_64 (returns 8 where LLVM and the model return -8). A backend defect on a legal input, in every optimize mode.
